step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify the primary external entry point: 'UserConsumerMobile' (represented as mobile/desktop client icons).
2. Trace the front-end API path: Client requests go to API Gateway, which invokes a frontend Lambda function.
3. Trace the asynchronous rendering queuing flow: The frontend Lambda sends rendering instructions to an SQS queue (bottom), which EC2 Auto Scaling workers consume.
4. Trace the immediate response path: EC2 Auto Scaling workers send job confirmation/status to a response SQS queue (top), which the frontend Lambda reads to return a playlist link back to the Client.
5. Trace video storage and distribution: EC2 Auto Scaling renders and uploads video segments to S3, which CloudFront caches and serves to the Client device.
6. Trace auto-scaling mechanism: Step Functions triggers a scaling Lambda every 15 seconds, which reads CloudWatch metrics (pushed by EC2 Auto Scaling) and updates Auto Scaling capacity.
7. Trace spot instance interruption flow: CloudWatch Events detects spot interruption warnings, triggering an interruption Lambda that signals the affected EC2 instance to drain and detach.

graph.name: SundaySky Rendering as a Service Ecosystem
graph.notes: Architecture for SundaySky's personalized video Rendering as a Service (RaaS) using spot instances, SQS queues, Step Functions, and API Gateway.

nodes.name: Client Device (Mobile / PC)
nodes.notes: End-user device requesting personalized video rendering and watching playback

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Handles client rendering requests with usage plans and API keys

nodes.name: Frontend Lambda
nodes.notes: Validates render requests, manages job submission and response handling

nodes.name: Rendering Instruction SQS Queue
nodes.notes: Holds rendering instructions for engine workers

nodes.name: Response SQS Queue
nodes.notes: Receives quick responses from rendering engines

nodes.name: EC2 Auto Scaling (Engine Service)
nodes.notes: Fleet of EC2 spot instances performing video rendering jobs

nodes.name: CloudFront CDN
nodes.notes: Distributes video segments to end users

nodes.name: Scaling Lambda
nodes.notes: Calculates required rendering capacity and updates Auto Scaling Group

nodes.name: CloudWatch / Events
nodes.notes: Collects rendering metrics and handles spot interruption event notifications

nodes.name: Spot Interruption Handler Lambda
nodes.notes: Handles 2-minute spot interruption warnings to gracefully drain instances

edges.notes: Frontend Lambda pushes rendering instructions to SQS
EC2 instances pull rendering jobs from SQS queue
EC2 instance responds immediately with job response
Frontend Lambda pulls response from SQS
Frontend Lambda returns playlist URL to client device
EC2 instances render and upload video segments to S3
CloudFront fetches video segments from S3 origin
Client streams video segments via CloudFront
Step Functions triggers scaling Lambda every 15 seconds
Rendering instances push metrics to CloudWatch
Scaling Lambda adjusts capacity in Auto Scaling group
CloudWatch Events notifies spot interruption to handler Lambda
Handler Lambda signals instance to stop taking jobs and drain
